public_rationale: The December 2023 research account supports the contextual claim that foundation-model systems lacked the provenance support needed for reliable training-source manifests. Existing search citations are an important qualification: the sentence would be too broad if read as denying all source lists. The proposed support therefore applies to underlying-source manifests, as suggested by the surrounding discussion of training and provenance.
limitations: The outcome depends on the contextual meaning of “manifest”.
The decisive source is a technical synthesis published later and explicitly describing its December 2023 writing period.
It does not establish the separate causal claim that attribution was architecturally impossible.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Current generative AI systems do not give users a manifest of sources.

statement.excerpt: A good system should give the user a manifest of sources; current systems don’t.
statement.document_title: Things are about to get a lot worse for Generative AI

our_interpretation: Assess the factual second clause; the statement about what a good system should do is normative.
In the surrounding discussion, a manifest means a reliable account of the underlying source materials behind generated outputs, including training sources.
The ordinary contextual scope is mainstream foundation-model systems such as DALL-E and ChatGPT. A bibliography of retrieved pages is not necessarily a training-source manifest.
Use December 2023 as the latest contemporaneous capability snapshot before the post. This is a month-level description of the state at publication, not an assessment of later product changes.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence addressing December 2023 shows that mainstream systems did not provide users with reliable output-specific manifests of underlying training sources.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A mainstream system available at the time demonstrably provided such a manifest to users.
